# <span id="aanchor188"></span> FLOWCAL Configuration

Accessing this screen requires **Application Process – FLOWCAL Options** permissions.

The FLOWCAL Configuration screen contains several application level options for the administrator to configure. While these settings are generally configured during installation, an administrator has the ability to modify these settings as needed. These options are effective for the entire application and cannot be configured for individual systems when licensed with the Multi-System Extension add-on.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 609;height: 446;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />FLOWCAL Configuration Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the FLOWCAL Configuration screen:

- **Close Schedule Type** - Determines the type of close schedule to be utilized by the monthly close process.
  - Selecting List (Default) will limit the object drop-down in the Close Schedules screen to lists.

  - Selecting Close Group will limit the object drop-down in the Close Schedules screen to close groups.

    When "Close Group" is selected, and if the "Require on Meter Create" option is checked, a close group must be assigned when creating a new meter from the Meter Editor (or Meter Quick Create for gas meters); otherwise, the meter cannot be saved.

    Close groups are created in the Close Group Editor under the main Setup menu. Users can then add meters to a close group by selecting the preferred close group under the close group drop-down within the Meter Editor.

- **GQ Apply Range** - This option is used in conjunction with the "Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited" option within the quality source assignment for gas meters only.

  By default, "No Limit" is selected, which enables a source assignment to look back as far as the beginning of time on a quality source when applying a sample.

  Unchecking the No Limit option and selecting a range (number of days, months, or years) limits how far back to look for a sample on the quality source during a source apply. If the end date of a sample is farther back in time from the start date of the record than the specified range, then the sample will not be applied. This will prevent applying an analysis that is older than the allowed time between samples.

  Checking the No Limit option or specifying a large (or long) time frame for the Range can result in performance issues due to the increased processing load that may be required.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  A company may be contractually obligated to pull samples at least once a year for all sample points. If the Range is set to 13 months to give field technicians a month’s grace period, then once the sample becomes 13 months old, FLOWCAL will stop applying it.

  </div>

- **<span id="Subtotal"></span>Subtotal by Meter Direction** - When checked, location rollups total data by meter direction in addition to calculating the total gain or loss for the location.

  In the Location Final Form tables, this will generate in an extra record per meter direction. The results can be viewed in the Daily and Monthly Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Analysis viewers.

- **<span id="SubtotalClass"></span>Subtotal by Meter Class** - When "Subtotal by Meter Direction" is selected, the Subtotal by "Meter Class" option becomes enabled. When checked, location rollups subtotal data by meter class in addition to meter direction.

  In the Location Final Form tables, this will generate in an extra record per meter class for each meter direction. Totals by meter class and direction can be viewed in the Daily and Monthly Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Analysis viewers.

  Class is subordinate to direction. FLOWCAL ships with several pre-defined meter directions and classes, but you can define unique directions and classes. This allows for the creation of directions that conform to company standard naming conventions and allows you to classify the use of a meter.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Subtotal">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  If you have a location with inlet and outlet meters all with class of Fuel, there will be a subtotal record in the Location Final Form table for Inlets\Fuels and Outlets\Fuels as well as a grand total for the Fuels class.

  </div>

- **Station Member Required** - When checked, station locations created in the Location Editor must have at least one meter member.

- **Meter Association Required** - When checked, meters must be a member of a station location.

- **Disable Exception “Acknowledge” When Severity \>** - Used to prevent users from ignoring exceptions with a severity greater than the one specified. This is useful if there are certain exceptions that should always require user intervention to resolve, rather than just acknowledging it.

  Exception severity is defined in the Exception Description Editor. By default, all exceptions have a severity of one.

  The maximum exception severity is 5. By leaving the level at 5 for this field, any exception can be ignored.

- **<span id="GasLossTicket"></span>Gas Loss Ticket Direction** - Gas loss tickets must have a base direction of Outlet, which is used to define the contribution when calculating location balances totals. The user can create user-defined directions in the Meter Direction Editor, but only directions with a base direction of Outlet will be available for selection. The direction is reflected on the gas loss ticket.

- **DB Profile Name** - Oracle profiles control password complexity, expiration, re-use, and various quotas. By default, this is left blank and the Default Oracle profile is used. You can define a different Oracle profile that will be used for new FLOWCAL users by providing the profile name here.

  FLOWCAL will fail to operate properly if you specify a profile that does not exist in the Oracle database instance.

- **Observed Density Tolerance** - FLOWCAL calculates observed density by multiplying the density meter factor (DMF) by the uncorrected density. All three values can be imported in a CFX or TFX file. If all three values are imported, FLOWCAL will calculate an observed density and compare it to the imported observed density. If the difference is more than the value defined for Observed Density Tolerance, an exception is generated.

  Entry is limited to a maximum of 1.

- **Ticket Date Populates** - Tickets, for a product movement (ex. scales, meters, rail car) have three dates: Effective Date, Movement Start Date and Movement End Date. This option can help reduce analyst entry time and reduce errors by automatically copying the Effective Date to the Movement Start Date or End Date when a date is not provided.
  - If this option is set to "Movement Start Date", then when the Effective Date is entered, if the Movement Start Date is undefined, the Effective Date is copied to the Movement Start Date.
  - If it is set to "Movement End Date", then when the Effective Date is entered, if the Movement End Date is undefined, the Effective Date is copied to the Movement End Date.
  - If it is set to "Nothing", then entering the Effective Date does not populate the other two dates.

- **Default Liquid Recalc Method** - This option presets all liquid data editors (e.g., Volume Editor, the Ticket Editor and Source Assignments) to a default recalculation method for editing data. However, you are still able to select a different recalculation from the default when editing data. Options are:
  - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates volume and mass using the correlation factor.
  - **Correlation Factor** - Recalculates the correlation factor.
  - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates volume and mass and sets the correlation factor to 1.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ticket Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Ticket Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Options">

Product movements such as truck loads and unloads as well as inventory measurements such as tank gauges can be imported. On import, the user can specify a multitude of fields for each ticket, such as the customer, the transporter, the shipper, the destination and the origin. These values may not exist in FLOWCAL for that field. This is common when tickets are being generated at remote sites. A driver may pull in and be unable to find the applicable customer. The driver may be able to create one in the terminal management software at the site. This value will then be fed to FLOWCAL on import.

Should FLOWCAL create the shipper or import the ticket without the shipper on it and generate an exception? Ticket Options allow the user to tell FLOWCAL what to do in this situation.

For the end user, there should be a discussion about how to handle when a new entity, such as new customer, imports into FLOWCAL. For some, having FLOWCAL create a customer could be convenient. For other companies, they may choose to generate a message or exception and manually create the new ticket item. Once these values are created, they cannot be removed from FLOWCAL without purging the ticket or meter data as they are then part of the audit trail. This would mean that the user could have Flow-Cal, FlowCal, FlowCAL and FLOWCAL for the same company.

Once the product, shipper, customer, transporter, facility, destination or origin is in FLOWCAL, it is part of the audit trail, unless all data that references it is purged out. When the product is created, a system message will be created.

The following items are available in Ticket Options:

- **Create Revisions** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, ticket data is imported as a new revision if a record already exists with the same Host ID and Ticket ID. Host ID is the generator of the ticket and is defined in the import file. Ticket ID is unique per host and is defined in the import file.

- **Create Products** - Applicable for tickets and batches. When checked, if a product is not recognized on import, the product is created. Product configuration information will be imported. If the full product configuration information is not available on import, then calculations will not occur. The product will need to be set up in FLOWCAL and then the applicable records will need to be recalculated with a manual edit. For customers who have a limited product set, this option is not normally recommended.

- **Create Customers** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a customer does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the customer will be created in FLOWCAL. The new customer is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The customer is then visible in the Company Editor.

- **Create Shippers** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a shipper does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the shipper will be created in FLOWCAL. The new shipper is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The shipper is then visible in the Company Editor with Shipper checked. If the shipper already exists in the Company Editor, but Shipper is not checked, then the Shipper field for that customer will be checked.

- **Create Transporters** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a transporter does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the transporter will be created in FLOWCAL. The new transporter is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The transporter is then visible in the Company Editor with Transporter checked.

  If the shipper already exists in the Company Editor, but Transporter is not checked, then the Transporter field for that customer will be checked.

- **Create Destinations and Origins** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a destination or origin does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the destination or origin will be created in FLOWCAL.

- **Create Facilities** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a From Facility or a To Facility does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the facility will be created in FLOWCAL. The new facility is then visible in the Facility Editor.

- **Use Ticket ID as BOL If Not Provided (At Import Only)** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, the BOL (Bill of Lading) on a ticket is set to match the Ticket ID on import, when a BOL is not provided. Note: Ticket ID is not visible to the user in FLOWCAL. It will be generated by the system that generates the import file and must be unique. The Ticket ID plus the unique name of the system makes each ticket unique in FLOWCAL. This allows FLOWCAL to determine when importing a ticket if the ticket has been imported before or if it is a revision.

- **Use Ticket ID as Ticket Number (At Import Only)** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, Ticket Number is set to match the Ticket ID on import. When not checked, the Ticket Number will follow the settings for the ‘Generate Ticket Number at’ option.

- **Allow Entry of Uncorrected Density** - Uncorrected density can be imported for batch meters and meter tickets. When checked, you can manually enter or edit the uncorrected density. Typically, this is for companies who do not enter the DMF into their flow computers in the field and need FLOWCAL to calculate the corrected density. If you do not need to enter uncorrected density, leave this box unchecked to reduce the chance of another user entering a density value in the wrong field.

- **Allow Edit of CTPL** - CTPL can be imported for batch meters and meter tickets and can also be calculated. When checked, you can manually enter or edit the Correction for Temperature and Pressure of the Liquid (CTPL). When this value is edited, the calculation of the Combined Correction Factor (CCF) becomes CCF = CTPL \* meter factor where meter factor is rounded per product discrimination rules. Correction for Temperature of the Liquid (CTL) and Correction for Pressure of the Liquid (CPL) will still be calculated as they normally would, but they will not be used in the calculation of the CCF. Check this option only if there is a need to override the imported or calculated CTPL.

- **Use Rounded CTPL in CCF** - Applicable for tickets and meters.

  - API defines CCF to be calculated as follows:  
    Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z).

  <!-- -->

  - When checked, CCF is calculated as follows:  
    Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z),w).

  This option does not conform to API 12.2.2.

- **<span id="Generate"></span>Generate Ticket Number at** - You can determine when ticket numbers for batches or tickets are created.

  - **New** - When the batch is first created on import or manual entry.
  - **Save** - When the batch data is saved after import or manual entry.
  - **Close** - When the batch data is closed for the month.

  These options are used in conjunction to further determine when ticket numbers are created.

  - **Assign Ticket Number as Needed (Only if Missing)** – A ticket number is assigned to a batch or ticket on import or edit if one is not specified.
  - **Always Assign Ticket Numbers (Overwrite Existing)** – A ticket number is always assigned to a batch or ticket, replacing the imported value. This will ensure ticket numbers are unique.
  - **Do Not Assign Ticket Numbers** - Ticket number must be manually assigned or provided on import.

- **Batch Number is Unique** - You can determine how ticket numbers for batches or tickets are created.
  - **Globally** - When selected, a unique value is used for each batch and ticket when FLOWCAL assigns a ticket number. This ensures that each ticket number is completely unique. The length can be controlled from the configuration file fcdebugoptions (contact Customer Support for additional information) 
  - **Per Meter** - When selected, ticket numbers are unique only by appending the meter number to the ticket number. For example, meter ABC and meter XYZ both have ticket numbers of 000001. Only by concatenating the meter number to the ticket number (e.g. ABC000001) is there a unique identifier.

- **Allow User to Edit Ticket Number** - Applicable for tickets and batches. When checked, you can manually edit the ticket number when entering or editing a batch in the Volume Editor or when entering or editing a ticket in the Ticket Editor.

- **Include CPA on Batch Ticket** - Applicable for batches only. Current period adjustments (CPA) are calculated for a batch when a prove is manually applied to a meter batch in the Volume Editor. The CPA is the change in mass or volume based on prove factor changes. When checked, the CPA amount will be displayed on printed tickets. If the printing of CPAs on tickets is not desired, then do not check this option.

- **Show Off Spec on Batch Tickets** - Applicable to tickets only, and not to meter batches. When checked, if product specification validations fail for the ticket, printed tickets will show that the data is off spec and will print on the report which components are out of bounds, what the value is, and what the limit is.

  See additional information on the following reports:

  - [Ticket Detail](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#TicketDetail) and [Ticket Detail Allowables](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#TicketDetailAllowables)
  - [Final Form Ticket](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Other%20Application%20Reports.md#FinalFormTicket) and [Final Form Ticket Allowed](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Other%20Application%20Reports.md#FinalFormTicketAllowed)

- **Use SPLC Code for Origins and Destinations** - Standard Point Location Codes (SPLC) are nine-digit codes used in North America by various shippers. Every location has an SPLC code defined by the location’s city, county (or parish) and state. When checked, an SPLC code can be entered into the Origin/Destination Editor along with city, county and state. The SPLC Code must be a number. When unchecked, then origins and destinations will be string fields (e.g., League City, TX) on tickets. Origins and destinations can be imported or manually entered.

- **Enforce Tickets Received in Order** - Applicable for tickets. Ticket imports contain a sequence number associated to each ticket ID.

  When checked, FLOWCAL validates that each imported ticket has the next sequence number on import. The first ticket for a given ticket ID must have a sequence number of 0.

  The next ticket for that ticket ID must have a sequence number of 1. However, if the next ticket for a given ticket ID has a sequence number other than what is expected, the ticket is not imported, and an exception is generated.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Capacity Table Import">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Capacity Table Import</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Capacity Table Import">

The Ticket Recalc Method is the default recalculation method that will be used when tank capacity tables and configuration options are edited. Users can choose an alternate method when editing the ticket. Options are:

- **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Volumetric and mass quantities are recalculated using the correlation factors.
- **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Correlation factors are recalculated; volumetric and mass quantities are left unchanged.
- **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Correlation factors are forced to 1 and volumetric and mass quantities are then calculated.
- **No Recalc** - Changes are saved and no recalculation takes place. This option is generally discouraged as this forces supporting data to be out of sync with the resulting quantities.

</div>
